text_for_scoring: Survived Irma on Anguilla. Complete devastation here. We had a harrowing early morning yesterday as Irma swept past us over 8 hours. Sustained winds up to 185mph and gusts in the 200s. The most terrifying experience of my life, and I've been through 10 hurricanes before. For all of you in Florida, please stay safe. This storm will be one for the ages. If you have even the slightest misgivings about where you are planning to hole up, please LEAVE! Here it's picked up semi-trailers and containers and planted them upside down. Cars thrown about like toys. CBS homes pretty much exploding from the pressure build up after roofs or a window went. Our plywood was stripped clean off all our windows. Metal roller shutters stripped clean off others. TL; DR - if you live in a stick-framed house, you need to go elsewhere.
label: High RPI

text_for_scoring: I'd rather have people panicked than not taking ANY hurricane seriously. I experienced Hugo and Charley first hand, and was in the cone for several of the storms that hit FL in 2004. Grew up in SC, then moved to FL, so I should be used to storms by now, but 2004 gave me hurricane PTSD. I moved inland more to get away from the storms, but it seems this is a hotspot for them, and we always get some outer bands. I don't freak out, but I am always concerned, because hurricanes are so unpredictable. My advice to everyone is to prepare as best you can and watch the forecast carefully. If they tell you to evacuate, dammit, do it! People die because they don't take hurricanes seriously enough, or they want to stay and protect their property. You can buy more stuff. Last time I checked, you can't buy a new life, or new children. During Andrew, one man who refused to evacuate and made his family stay with him had the wind rip the plywood off of his window and a 2x4 flew in and hit his 12 yo child in the head, killing her. Another had his pregnant wife sitting in the bathtub praying for her life. I keep telling people this, but no one listens. If they tell you to leave, JUST LEAVE!! I watched Hurricane Michael completely bury homes in water in the Panhandle. I'll never forget that one man was live streaming from a 2 story house on 12-foot stilts, and water was lapping at his door. He showed a picture of his neighbor's house, not on stilts, with water up almost over the roof, and said they hadn't evacuated. I remember people sifting through the rubble searching for bodies for days, some of the missing were never found, likely washed out to sea. Mexico Beach, FL was completely wiped off the face of the earth. NEVER EVER think you can outsmart a hurricane. Even with a Cat. 1, it's not the wind, it's the water that kills.
label: High vulnerable
